0.name: Not Relevant
0.definition: The CV has no meaningful alignment with the core requirements of the JD.
criteria: Completely different industry and role with no transferable experience

1.name: Low Relevance
1.definition: The CV has some related skills or experience but does not satisfy important requirements.
criteria: Some skill overlap but missing most core requirements
Related industry but different role specialization
Entry-level experience for a position requiring significant experience
Transferable soft skills but lacking technical requirements

2.name: Relevant
2.definition: The CV satisfies most core requirements, with some gaps in preferred skills or experience.
criteria: Relevant role experience in similar domain

3.name: Highly Relevant
3.definition: The CV demonstrates strong alignment with the required skills, responsibilities, and relevant experience.
criteria: Meets all or nearly all must-have skills
Strong relevant experience in the same or closely related role

required_skills.name: Required Skills
required_skills.description: Whether the candidate demonstrates the skills required by the JD.

matching_levels.equivalent: Different name but same skill (e.g., PostgreSQL = Postgres)
matching_levels.related: Related or transferable skill in the same family
matching_levels.insufficient: No clear evidence of the skill

role_responsibilities.name: Role and Responsibilities
role_responsibilities.description: Whether the candidate's previous work experience is relevant to the target job.

experience_seniority.name: Experience and Seniority
experience_seniority.description: Years of experience and seniority level alignment.
experience_seniority.note: Do not automatically reject candidates for missing years when the JD does not define a strict minimum.

industry_domain.name: Industry and Domain
industry_domain.note: Industry mismatch should not automatically imply irrelevance.

preferred_skills.name: Preferred Skills
preferred_skills.description: Additional skills listed as preferred or nice-to-have.
preferred_skills.note: Should not have the same penalty as missing mandatory requirements.

evidence_states.present: The CV contains evidence of the skill or qualification.
evidence_states.absent: There is sufficient evidence that the candidate does not meet the criterion.
evidence_states.unknown: The CV does not provide enough information to determine whether the candidate meets the criterion. Absence of a skill in the CV does not necessarily prove the candidate does not possess it.

hard_constraint.definition: Explicit mandatory conditions that cannot reasonably be substituted, such as legally required certifications or clearly non-negotiable conditions.

soft_criterion.definition: Skills, responsibilities, experience, seniority, industry, and preferred qualifications that can be assessed by degree of alignment.

vn_to_common_thresholds.description: Map Vietnamese LLM consensus scores (1-9 scale, median of 3 models) to the common 0-3 relevance rubric.
vn_to_common_thresholds.boundary_handling: Boundary values (2.5, 4.5, 6.5) are assigned to the higher category. This is a conditional mapping that should be validated against human-annotated samples.
